rules.rule_name: BR-001: Detect First-Time Application Launch
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the user is accessing the Sign-On screen for the first time (no active session exists) or returning after a prior interaction, and routes accordingly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: First Time Launch? EIBCALEN = 0

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the CardDemo Sign-On application
acceptance_criteria.When: No prior session communication area exists (first-time launch)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system initializes the screen output area to low values, positions the cursor on the User ID field, and displays the Sign-On screen for the first time

rules.rule_name: BR-002: Populate Sign-On Screen Header Information
rules.rule_description: Every time the Sign-On screen is rendered, the header section must be populated with current date, current time, application titles, transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 2: Populate Screen Header Information

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Sign-On screen is about to be displayed to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for rendering
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), current Transaction Name (WS-TRANID), current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME), current date formatted as MM/DD/YY (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY), current time formatted as HH:MM:SS (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS), the Application ID (APPLID), and the System ID (SYSID)

rules.rule_name: BR-003: Display Sign-On Screen to User
rules.rule_description: The Sign-On screen is sent to the user's terminal with any error messages and cursor positioning applied, clearing the previous screen content before display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 1: Display Signon Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen header has been populated and any applicable error message has been set in WS-MESSAGE
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the Sign-On screen (COSGN0A / COSGN00) to the terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error message field (ERRMSGO) on the screen is populated with WS-MESSAGE, the screen is sent with ERASE to clear prior content, the cursor is positioned as specified, and the system waits for the next user input

rules.rule_name: BR-004: Handle User Key Press Selection
rules.rule_description: When a returning user interacts with the Sign-On screen, the system evaluates which key was pressed and routes to the appropriate processing path: ENTER for login, PF3 for exit, or any other key triggers an invalid key error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 3: Handle User Keypress

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has an active session and is on the Sign-On screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses a key and the system receives the input
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the key is ENTER, the system proceeds to validate the login credentials; if the key is PF3, the system displays a Thank You message and ends the session; if any other key is pressed, the system sets an error flag and displays the invalid key error message

rules.rule_name: BR-005: Exit Application with Thank You Message on PF3
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 on the Sign-On screen, the application displays a Thank You message and terminates the current session without returning to the Sign-On transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 14: Exit Application with Thank You Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Sign-On screen with an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the standard Thank You message (CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU) as plain text on the screen, clears the screen (ERASE), releases the keyboard (FREEKB), and immediately ends the session with no further transaction return

rules.rule_name: BR-006: Handle Invalid Key Press on Sign-On Screen
rules.rule_description: If the user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3 on the Sign-On screen, the system rejects the action and informs the user that the key pressed is not valid.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 13: Handle Invalid Key Press

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Sign-On screen with an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), populates WS-MESSAGE with the invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message shown in the ERRMSGO field

rules.rule_name: BR-007: Validate User ID is Not Blank
rules.rule_description: The User ID field is mandatory on the Sign-On screen. If the user submits the form without entering a User ID, the system must reject the submission and prompt the user to provide one.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 4: Validate User ID Entry

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user presses ENTER on the Sign-On screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID field (USERIDI of COSGN0AI) contains only spaces or low values (is blank or empty)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets WS-MESSAGE to 'Please enter User ID ...', positions the cursor on the User ID field (USERIDL = -1), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message; no further login processing occurs

rules.rule_name: BR-008: Validate Password is Not Blank
rules.rule_description: The Password field is mandatory on the Sign-On screen. If the user submits the form with a valid User ID but without entering a Password, the system must reject the submission and prompt the user to provide one.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 5: Validate Password Entry

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user presses ENTER on the Sign-On screen and has entered a valid (non-blank) User ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The Password field (PASSWDI of COSGN0AI) contains only spaces or low values (is blank or empty)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets WS-MESSAGE to 'Please enter Password ...', positions the cursor on the Password field (PASSWDL = -1), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message; no further login processing occurs

rules.rule_name: BR-009: Normalize User Credentials to Uppercase
rules.rule_description: Before performing any authentication lookup, both the User ID and Password entered by the user are converted to uppercase to ensure case-insensitive credential matching.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 6: Normalize User Credentials to Uppercase

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered both a non-blank User ID and a non-blank Password on the Sign-On screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the credentials for authentication
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID (USERIDI of COSGN0AI) is converted to uppercase and stored in both WS-USER-ID and CDEMO-USER-ID; the Password (PASSWDI of COSGN0AI) is converted to uppercase and stored in WS-USER-PWD; these uppercase values are used for all subsequent authentication processing

rules.rule_name: BR-010: Look Up User in Security File
rules.rule_description: The system retrieves the user's security record from the User Security File (USRSEC) using the normalized (uppercase) User ID as the lookup key, provided no prior validation errors have occurred.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 7: Look Up User in Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has provided a non-blank User ID and Password, both have been normalized to uppercase, and no validation errors have been flagged (ERR-FLG-ON is false)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a lookup on the User Security File (WS-USRSEC-FILE) using WS-USER-ID as the key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the user's security record (SEC-USER-DATA) including the stored password (SEC-USR-PWD) and user type (SEC-USR-TYPE) for use in subsequent authentication steps

rules.rule_name: BR-011: Handle User Not Found in Security File
rules.rule_description: If the entered User ID does not exist in the User Security File, the system informs the user that the account was not found and prompts them to try again.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 9: Handle User Not Found

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup on the User Security File using the entered User ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID is not found in the User Security File (response code = 13 / record not found)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets WS-MESSAGE to 'User not found. Try again ...', positions the cursor on the User ID field (USERIDL = -1), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message

rules.rule_name: BR-012: Handle Authentication System Error
rules.rule_description: If an unexpected condition occurs while attempting to retrieve the user's record from the security file, the system informs the user that verification could not be completed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 10: Handle Authentication System Error

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup on the User Security File using the entered User ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The security file lookup returns an unexpected error (any response code other than success or record-not-found)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets WS-MESSAGE to 'Unable to verify the User ...', positions the cursor on the User ID field (USERIDL = -1), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message

rules.rule_name: BR-013: Verify User Password Against Stored Credentials
rules.rule_description: When a user record is successfully found in the security file, the system compares the entered (uppercase) password against the stored password to authenticate the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 8: Verify User Password

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user's record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the entered password (WS-USER-PWD, already normalized to uppercase) against the stored password (SEC-USR-PWD) in the retrieved security record
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the passwords match, the system proceeds to establish the user session and route the user; if the passwords do not match, the system displays a wrong password error

rules.rule_name: BR-014: Handle Wrong Password Entry
rules.rule_description: If the user is found in the security file but the entered password does not match the stored password, the system rejects the login and prompts the user to try again.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Wrong Password Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user's record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered password (WS-USER-PWD) does not match the stored password (SEC-USR-PWD)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets WS-MESSAGE to 'Wrong Password. Try again ...', positions the cursor on the Password field (PASSWDL = -1), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message; no session is established

rules.rule_name: BR-015: Establish User Session Context on Successful Authentication
rules.rule_description: Upon successful authentication (User ID found and password matches), the system records the session context information that will be passed to downstream application programs.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 8: Verify User Password

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user's record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File and the entered password matches the stored password
acceptance_criteria.When: Authentication is confirmed as successful
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the following in the shared session context (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA): the originating Transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID = WS-TRANID), the originating Program Name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM = WS-PGMNAME), the authenticated User ID (CDEMO-USER-ID = WS-USER-ID), the User Type (CDEMO-USER-TYPE = SEC-USR-TYPE), and the Program Context is reset to zero (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = 0)

rules.rule_name: BR-016: Route Admin User to Administration Menu
rules.rule_description: After successful authentication, if the user is identified as an Administrator, the system transfers control to the Administration Menu program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 11: Route Admin User to Administration Menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated (User ID found and password matched) and the session context has been established
acceptance_criteria.When: The user's type (CDEMO-USER-TYPE / SEC-USR-TYPE) is identified as ADMIN (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is true)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Administration Menu program (COADM01C), passing the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)

rules.rule_name: BR-017: Route Regular User to Main Menu
rules.rule_description: After successful authentication, if the user is not an Administrator, the system transfers control to the Regular User Main Menu program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 12: Route Regular User to Main Menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated (User ID found and password matched) and the session context has been established
acceptance_criteria.When: The user's type (CDEMO-USER-TYPE / SEC-USR-TYPE) is NOT identified as ADMIN (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is false)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Regular User Main Menu program (COMEN01C), passing the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)

rules.rule_name: Route to Login Validation on Enter Key Press
rules.rule_description: When the user presses the Enter key on the Sign-On screen, the system initiates the login validation process to authenticate the user's credentials.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Process Login Attempt Enter Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Sign-On screen and has pressed a key
acceptance_criteria.When: The key pressed is the Enter key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds to the login validation process to verify the user's entered credentials (User ID and Password)

rules.rule_name: Display Thank You Message and End Session on PF3 Key Press
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 on the Sign-On screen, the system displays a Thank You message and terminates the current application session immediately without returning to the Sign-On screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Thank You Message and Exit Application

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Sign-On screen and has pressed a key
acceptance_criteria.When: The key pressed is PF3
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the standard Thank You message (CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU) as plain text on the screen, the keyboard is unlocked for the user, and the application session is terminated — no further transaction processing occurs and the Sign-On screen is not redisplayed

rules.rule_name: Display Invalid Key Error and Redisplay Sign-On Screen
rules.rule_description: When the user presses any key other than Enter or PF3 on the Sign-On screen, the system flags an error, displays an invalid key error message, and redisplays the Sign-On screen so the user can retry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Invalid Key Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Sign-On screen and has pressed a key
acceptance_criteria.When: The key pressed is any key other than Enter or PF3
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', populates the error message area on the Sign-On screen with the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message visible so the user can press a valid key

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Sign-On Screen with Invalid Key Error
rules.rule_description: After an invalid key press is detected, the Sign-On screen is refreshed with updated header information (current date, time, application ID, system ID) and the invalid key error message displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redisplay Signon Screen with Error

acceptance_criteria.Given: An invalid key error has been flagged and the invalid key error message has been set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Sign-On screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with the current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID; the invalid key error message is placed in the error message field of the Sign-On screen; and the Sign-On screen is redisplayed with the error message visible, awaiting the next valid user input

rules.rule_name: Receive User Credentials from Sign-On Screen
rules.rule_description: When a user presses the Enter key on the Sign-On screen, the system captures the User ID and Password entered by the user from the screen input fields.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Receive User ID and Password from Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Sign-On screen is displayed and the user has pressed the Enter key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads the Sign-On screen input
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures the values entered in the User ID field and the Password field from the screen for further validation

rules.rule_name: User ID Mandatory Validation
rules.rule_description: The system enforces that the User ID field must be populated before a login attempt can proceed. If the User ID is blank or empty, the login attempt is rejected with an appropriate error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is User ID Blank or Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key on the Sign-On screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID field is blank or empty (contains spaces or low values)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'Please enter User ID ...', repositions the cursor to the User ID field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen. The login attempt does not proceed further.

rules.rule_name: Password Mandatory Validation
rules.rule_description: The system enforces that the Password field must be populated before a login attempt can proceed. If the Password is blank or empty, the login attempt is rejected with an appropriate error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Password Blank or Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key on the Sign-On screen and the User ID field has been successfully validated as non-blank
acceptance_criteria.When: The Password field is blank or empty (contains spaces or low values)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'Please enter Password ...', repositions the cursor to the Password field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen. The login attempt does not proceed further.

rules.rule_name: Uppercase Conversion of User Credentials
rules.rule_description: To ensure case-insensitive authentication, the system converts both the User ID and Password to uppercase before performing any lookup or comparison against stored credentials.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Convert User ID and Password to Uppercase

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a non-blank User ID and a non-blank Password on the Sign-On screen
acceptance_criteria.When: Both the User ID and Password fields pass the mandatory field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system converts the entered User ID to uppercase and stores it as the active User ID for the session lookup. The system also converts the entered Password to uppercase for subsequent password matching. The uppercase User ID is also stored in the shared session communication area.

rules.rule_name: User Identity Lookup in Security File
rules.rule_description: The system searches the User Security File using the uppercase User ID to retrieve the user's stored security record, including stored password and user type, for authentication purposes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Search User Security File Using User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User ID and Password have been validated as non-blank and converted to uppercase
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a lookup of the User Security File using the uppercase User ID as the search key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the user's security record from the User Security File if the User ID exists, or returns an appropriate status indicating the user was not found or a system error occurred

rules.rule_name: User Not Found in Security File
rules.rule_description: If the entered User ID does not exist in the User Security File, the system rejects the login attempt and prompts the user to try again.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: User Not Found

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has searched the User Security File using the entered User ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID is not found in the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'User not found. Try again ...', repositions the cursor to the User ID field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen. The login attempt is rejected.

rules.rule_name: System Unable to Verify User Identity
rules.rule_description: If the system encounters an unexpected condition while attempting to verify the user's identity in the Security File, the login attempt is rejected and the user is informed that verification could not be completed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: System Error

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to search the User Security File using the entered User ID
acceptance_criteria.When: An unexpected system condition occurs during the user lookup that is neither a successful retrieval nor a 'user not found' condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'Unable to verify the User ...', repositions the cursor to the User ID field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen. The login attempt is rejected.

rules.rule_name: Password Match Validation Against Stored Credentials
rules.rule_description: After the user record is successfully retrieved from the Security File, the system validates that the password entered by the user matches the password stored in the user's security record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does Entered Password Match Stored Password?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User ID has been found in the User Security File and the user's security record has been retrieved
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the uppercase-converted entered password against the stored password in the user's security record
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the passwords do not match, the system displays the message 'Wrong Password. Try again ...', repositions the cursor to the Password field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen. The login attempt is rejected. If the passwords match, the system proceeds to establish the user session.

rules.rule_name: Establish User Session Information on Successful Authentication
rules.rule_description: Upon successful authentication, the system records the user's session context information in the shared communication area so that downstream programs can identify the authenticated user and their role throughout the session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set User Session Information: Transaction ID, Program Name, User ID, User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has been successfully authenticated with a matching User ID and Password
acceptance_criteria.When: Authentication is confirmed as successful
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the following session information in the shared communication area: the originating Transaction ID, the originating Program Name, the authenticated User ID, the User Type (Admin or Regular), and resets the Program Context to zero to indicate a fresh program start

rules.rule_name: Route Authenticated Admin User to Administration Menu
rules.rule_description: After successful authentication, if the user is identified as an Administrator, the system routes them to the Administration Menu program, passing the established session context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Yes - Admin User

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has been successfully authenticated and the session context has been established
acceptance_criteria.When: The user's type stored in the Security File is identified as Administrator (Admin)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Administration Menu program (COADM01C), passing the full session communication area, so the Admin user can access administrative functions

rules.rule_name: Route Authenticated Regular User to Main Menu
rules.rule_description: After successful authentication, if the user is identified as a Regular (non-Admin) user, the system routes them to the Main Menu program, passing the established session context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - Regular User

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has been successfully authenticated and the session context has been established
acceptance_criteria.When: The user's type stored in the Security File is identified as a Regular user (non-Admin)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Main Menu program (COMEN01C), passing the full session communication area, so the Regular user can access standard application functions

rules.rule_name: User ID Presence Validation on Signon Screen Submission
rules.rule_description: When a user submits the signon screen by pressing Enter, the system must verify that the User ID field has been filled in. If the User ID field is empty or contains only blank spaces, the submission is rejected and the user is prompted to provide a User ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is User ID Field Empty or Blank?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has accessed the signon screen and presses the Enter key to submit their credentials
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID field submitted on the signon screen is empty or contains only blank spaces
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system rejects the login attempt, sets an error indicator to active, displays the error message 'Please enter User ID ...', repositions the cursor to the User ID field, and redisplays the signon screen with the error message so the user can re-enter their credentials

rules.rule_name: Activate Error Indicator on Missing User ID
rules.rule_description: When the User ID field is found to be empty or blank upon signon screen submission, the system must activate an internal error indicator to signal that a validation failure has occurred, preventing any further authentication processing from taking place.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Indicator

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the signon screen by pressing Enter
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID field is empty or blank
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error indicator flag to 'Y' (active/on), which prevents any downstream authentication or user lookup from being executed for this submission

rules.rule_name: Display User ID Missing Error Message
rules.rule_description: When the User ID field is empty or blank on signon screen submission, the system must prepare and display a specific, user-friendly error message instructing the user to enter their User ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Prepare Error Message: 'Please enter User ID...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the signon screen by pressing Enter and the User ID field is empty or blank
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects the missing User ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system prepares the error message 'Please enter User ID ...' to be displayed on the signon screen so the user understands exactly what information is required

rules.rule_name: Reposition Cursor to User ID Field on Validation Failure
rules.rule_description: When the User ID field is found to be empty or blank, the system must automatically reposition the screen cursor to the User ID input field to guide the user directly to the field that requires attention, improving the user experience.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reposition Cursor to User ID Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the signon screen by pressing Enter and the User ID field is empty or blank
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the signon screen with the error message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the cursor position to the User ID input field so that when the signon screen is redisplayed, the cursor is automatically placed in the User ID field, ready for the user to type their User ID

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Signon Screen with User ID Error
rules.rule_description: After detecting a missing User ID and preparing the error message and cursor position, the system must redisplay the signon screen including the header information (current date, time, application details) along with the error message, so the user can correct their input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redisplay Signon Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has detected that the User ID field is empty or blank, set the error indicator, prepared the error message 'Please enter User ID ...', and positioned the cursor on the User ID field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the signon screen back to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID, then displays the signon screen with the error message 'Please enter User ID ...' visible and the cursor positioned on the User ID field, awaiting the user's corrected input

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Password Validation When User ID is Present
rules.rule_description: When the User ID field contains a value (is not empty or blank), the signon screen submission passes the User ID validation check and the system proceeds to the next step of validating the Password field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Password Validation

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the signon screen by pressing Enter
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID field contains a non-blank, non-empty value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does not set an error for the User ID field and proceeds to validate whether the Password field has also been filled in

rules.rule_name: Password Field Mandatory Entry Validation
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Password field is not left blank or empty when the user submits the Sign-On screen. This ensures the user provides a password before the system attempts to authenticate their credentials.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Password Field Blank or Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has accessed the Sign-On screen and has pressed the ENTER key to submit the form, and the User ID field has already been validated as non-empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The Password field submitted on the Sign-On screen contains only blank spaces or is empty (LOW-VALUES)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to indicate a validation failure, (2) display the error message 'Please enter Password...' on the Sign-On screen, (3) reposition the cursor to the Password field so the user can immediately enter their password, and (4) redisplay the Sign-On screen with the error message visible, awaiting re-entry from the user

rules.rule_name: Password Entry Error Flag Activation
rules.rule_description: When the Password field is found to be blank or empty upon form submission, the system activates an error flag to signal that a validation failure has occurred, preventing any further credential verification or authentication processing from taking place.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Flag

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Sign-On screen by pressing ENTER, and the User ID field has passed its mandatory entry check
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects that the Password field is blank or empty (contains only spaces or LOW-VALUES)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the internal error flag to 'Y' (error condition active), which will prevent any downstream credential lookup or authentication processing from being triggered for this submission

rules.rule_name: Password Missing Error Message Display
rules.rule_description: When the Password field is blank or empty, the system communicates a clear, user-friendly error message instructing the user to provide their password before resubmitting the Sign-On screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Message: 'Please enter Password...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Sign-On screen by pressing ENTER with the Password field left blank or empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The system identifies the Password field as blank or empty and prepares to redisplay the Sign-On screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the error message to exactly 'Please enter Password...' and display this message in the error message area of the Sign-On screen so the user is clearly informed of what is required

rules.rule_name: Cursor Repositioning to Password Field on Validation Failure
rules.rule_description: To improve user experience and guide the user to correct the missing input, the system automatically repositions the cursor to the Password field when the password entry validation fails, allowing the user to immediately begin typing their password without manually clicking or tabbing to the field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reposition Cursor to Password Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has detected that the Password field was blank or empty upon Sign-On screen submission
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Sign-On screen with the password validation error message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the cursor position indicator for the Password field to -1, which instructs the screen to place the cursor directly in the Password input field when the screen is redisplayed

rules.rule_name: Sign-On Screen Redisplay After Password Validation Failure
rules.rule_description: After detecting a missing password entry, the system redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message and updated cursor position, allowing the user to correct their input and resubmit. The screen header is refreshed with current date, time, application, and system information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redisplay Signon Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has set the error flag, error message 'Please enter Password...', and cursor position to the Password field due to a blank password submission
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the screen redisplay process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) populate the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID; (2) place the error message 'Please enter Password...' in the error message display area of the Sign-On screen; (3) redisplay the full Sign-On screen with the cursor positioned on the Password field; and (4) return control to the Sign-On transaction, awaiting the user's next input

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Credential Normalization When Password is Present
rules.rule_description: When the Password field contains a non-blank, non-empty value, the password validation check passes and the system proceeds to the next step of normalizing (converting to uppercase) both the User ID and Password before performing credential verification.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Normalize Credentials

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Sign-On screen by pressing ENTER, and both the User ID and Password fields contain non-blank, non-empty values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the Password field and determines it is not blank or empty
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must allow processing to continue to the credential normalization step, where both the User ID and Password will be converted to uppercase in preparation for authentication against the user security records

rules.rule_name: Convert Entered User ID to Uppercase for Case-Insensitive Authentication
rules.rule_description: The system must normalize the User ID entered on the signon screen by converting it to uppercase before any authentication or security lookup is performed, ensuring that login is case-insensitive regardless of how the user typed their credentials.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Convert Entered User ID to Uppercase

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a User ID on the Signon Screen and pressed the ENTER key, and both the User ID and Password fields have been confirmed as non-blank
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the entered User ID prior to performing the security file lookup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system converts the entered User ID to uppercase and stores the normalized uppercase value as the active User ID to be used for all subsequent authentication processing

rules.rule_name: Store Uppercase User ID in Session Context for Downstream Use
rules.rule_description: After converting the User ID to uppercase, the system must store the normalized User ID in both the local authentication working area and the shared session context (communication area), so that the authenticated identity is consistently available to all downstream programs and menus after successful login.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store Uppercase User ID for Authentication

acceptance_criteria.Given: The entered User ID has been converted to uppercase
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the normalized User ID for use in authentication and session tracking
acceptance_criteria.Then: The uppercase User ID is stored in both the local authentication working storage field and the shared session context User ID field, ensuring the same normalized value is used for the security file lookup and carried forward into the session upon successful login

rules.rule_name: Convert Entered Password to Uppercase for Case-Insensitive Authentication
rules.rule_description: The system must normalize the Password entered on the signon screen by converting it to uppercase before comparing it against the stored password in the security file, ensuring that password validation is case-insensitive.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Convert Entered Password to Uppercase

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a Password on the Signon Screen and pressed the ENTER key, and both the User ID and Password fields have been confirmed as non-blank
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the entered Password prior to performing the security file lookup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system converts the entered Password to uppercase and stores the normalized uppercase value as the active Password to be used for all subsequent authentication and password comparison processing

rules.rule_name: Store Uppercase Password for Authentication Comparison
rules.rule_description: After converting the Password to uppercase, the system must store the normalized Password in the local authentication working area so it is ready to be compared against the password stored in the user security file during the authentication lookup.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store Uppercase Password for Authentication

acceptance_criteria.Given: The entered Password has been converted to uppercase
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the normalized Password for use in authentication
acceptance_criteria.Then: The uppercase Password is stored in the local authentication working storage field, and the system is ready to proceed to the security file lookup where this normalized password will be compared against the stored user password

rules.rule_name: Search User Security File by User ID
rules.rule_description: The system uses the entered User ID as the lookup key to search the User Security File and retrieve the corresponding user record containing the stored password and user type.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Search for User Record in Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a valid non-blank User ID and Password on the Sign-On screen and pressed ENTER
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a lookup on the User Security File (USRSEC) using the uppercase-converted User ID as the search key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the user record from the security file, which contains the stored password and user type, and proceeds to password verification

rules.rule_name: User Record Successfully Retrieved from Security File
rules.rule_description: When the User Security File lookup is successful, the system retrieves the full user record including the stored password and user type classification, which are then used for authentication and role-based routing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve User Record containing Stored Password and User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has searched the User Security File using the entered User ID as the key
acceptance_criteria.When: The user record is found successfully in the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the user record containing the stored password (SEC-USR-PWD) and the user type (SEC-USR-TYPE), and proceeds to password verification

rules.rule_name: User ID Does Not Exist in Security File
rules.rule_description: When the entered User ID cannot be found in the User Security File, the system rejects the login attempt, displays an appropriate error message, and prompts the user to re-enter their User ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: User Not Found: Display Error Message Re-prompt for User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has searched the User Security File using the entered User ID as the key
acceptance_criteria.When: No matching user record is found in the User Security File for the entered User ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'User not found. Try again...' on the Sign-On screen, repositions the cursor to the User ID field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen for re-entry

rules.rule_name: User Security File Cannot Be Accessed
rules.rule_description: When the User Security File is unavailable or returns an unexpected result during the user lookup, the system cannot verify the user's identity and displays an appropriate error message prompting the user to retry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: System Unavailable: Display Unable to Verify Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to search the User Security File using the entered User ID as the key
acceptance_criteria.When: The User Security File returns an unexpected or unrecognized response (neither a successful retrieval nor a user-not-found result)

rules.rule_name: Password Verification Against Stored Credentials
rules.rule_description: When a user record is successfully retrieved from the security file, the system compares the password entered by the user (converted to uppercase) against the stored password in the security file to determine whether authentication should proceed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does Entered Password Match Stored Password?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the user security file using the entered User ID, and both the entered User ID and Password have been converted to uppercase prior to comparison
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the uppercase-converted entered password (WS-USER-PWD) against the stored password (SEC-USR-PWD) retrieved from the user security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the entered password exactly matches the stored password, the system proceeds to prepare the user session information; if the passwords do not match, the system displays the error message 'Wrong Password. Try again...' and repositions the cursor to the Password field, then redisplays the Sign-On screen

rules.rule_name: Prepare User Session Context Upon Successful Authentication
rules.rule_description: Upon successful password verification, the system records all relevant session context information — including the originating transaction, program, authenticated user identity, and user type — into the shared communication area so that downstream programs can access this information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Prepare User Session Information:
- Record Transaction ID
- Record Program Name
- Confirm User ID
- Record User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: The entered password has been verified and matches the stored password in the user security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the session context for the authenticated user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the following into the shared session communication area: the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is stored as the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), the current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) is stored as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), the authenticated User ID (WS-USER-ID) is confirmed and stored (CDEMO-USER-ID), the User Type from the security file (SEC-USR-TYPE) is stored (CDEMO-USER-TYPE), and the program context is reset to zero (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = 0)

rules.rule_name: Determine User Role for Post-Login Routing
rules.rule_description: After session context is prepared, the system evaluates the authenticated user's type to determine whether the user holds an Administrator role, which governs which menu or application they are routed to after login.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is User an Administrator?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has been successfully authenticated and the session context has been fully populated with the user's transaction ID, program name, user ID, user type, and a reset program context
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the user type stored in the session context (CDEMO-USER-TYPE via CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN condition)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the user type is identified as Administrator (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is true), the system routes the user to the Administration Menu; if the user type is not Administrator (regular user), the system routes the user to the Main Menu

rules.rule_name: Route Administrator User to Administration Menu
rules.rule_description: When an authenticated user is identified as an Administrator, the system transfers control to the Administration Menu program, passing the fully populated session communication area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 11: Route to Administration Menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has been successfully authenticated with a matching password, the session context has been populated, and the user type is identified as Administrator (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is true)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the user holds the Administrator role
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Administration Menu program (COADM01C), passing the current session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the current program terminates its execution

rules.rule_name: Route Regular User to Main Menu
rules.rule_description: When an authenticated user is identified as a regular (non-Administrator) user, the system transfers control to the Main Menu program, passing the fully populated session communication area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 12: Route to Main Menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has been successfully authenticated with a matching password, the session context has been populated, and the user type is NOT identified as Administrator (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is false)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the user is a regular (non-Administrator) user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Main Menu program (COMEN01C), passing the current session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the current program terminates its execution

rules.rule_name: Wrong Password Error Notification and Screen Re-prompt
rules.rule_description: When the password entered by the user does not match the stored password in the security file, the system notifies the user with a specific error message, repositions the cursor to the Password field to facilitate correction, and redisplays the Sign-On screen for another attempt.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Error Message: 'Wrong Password. Try again...' / Reposition Cursor to Password Field / Signon Screen Redisplayed

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the user security file using the entered User ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The uppercase-converted entered password (WS-USER-PWD) does NOT match the stored password (SEC-USR-PWD) in the security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the error message 'Wrong Password. Try again...' on the Sign-On screen, repositions the cursor to the Password input field (PASSWDL of COSGN0AI set to -1), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the header information (current date, time, transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID) populated

rules.rule_name: Detect User ID Not Found in Security File
rules.rule_description: When a user attempts to sign on, the system looks up the entered User ID in the security file. If the User ID does not exist, the system must detect this condition and trigger the appropriate error handling flow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does User ID Exist in Security File?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a User ID and Password on the Sign-On screen and pressed ENTER, and both fields are non-blank
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a lookup of the entered User ID in the user security file and the User ID is NOT found (no matching record exists)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies that the User ID does not exist and initiates the 'User Not Found' error handling process

rules.rule_name: Activate Error Flag on User Not Found
rules.rule_description: When the User ID is not found in the security file, the system must activate the error flag to indicate that the current sign-on attempt has failed, preventing any further processing of the login.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Flag to Active

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the entered User ID in the user security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID is NOT found in the security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active ('Y'), marking the sign-on attempt as failed and blocking any further authentication processing

rules.rule_name: Prepare User Not Found Error Message
rules.rule_description: When the User ID entered by the user does not exist in the security file, the system must prepare a specific error message to inform the user that their User ID was not recognized and prompt them to try again.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Prepare Error Message: 'User not found. Try again...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the entered User ID does not exist in the user security file and the error flag has been set to active
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the error response for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error message to 'User not found. Try again ...' to be displayed on the Sign-On screen

rules.rule_name: Reposition Cursor to User ID Field on User Not Found
rules.rule_description: When the User ID is not found in the security file, the system must reposition the screen cursor back to the User ID input field, guiding the user to correct their User ID entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reposition Cursor to User ID Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the entered User ID does not exist in the user security file and has prepared the error message 'User not found. Try again ...'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Sign-On screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system repositions the cursor to the User ID input field so the user can immediately re-enter a valid User ID

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Sign-On Screen with User Not Found Error
rules.rule_description: After detecting that the User ID does not exist, the system must redisplay the Sign-On screen with the error message visible, the screen header refreshed with current date and time, and the cursor positioned at the User ID field so the user can re-enter their credentials.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redisplay Signon Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has set the error flag to active, prepared the error message 'User not found. Try again ...', and repositioned the cursor to the User ID field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system redisplays the Sign-On screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system refreshes the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID; displays the error message 'User not found. Try again ...' in the error message area of the Sign-On screen; clears the screen and positions the cursor at the User ID field; and waits for the user to re-enter their credentials

rules.rule_name: Detect Unexpected Security System Error During User Verification
rules.rule_description: When the user security file returns an unexpected or unrecognized response during a user lookup attempt, the system must flag an error condition to prevent further processing of the login request.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Security File Response - Unexpected System Error Occurred

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted their User ID and Password on the Sign-On screen and the system has attempted to look up the User ID in the user security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The security file returns a response that is neither a successful record found nor a record not found condition — indicating an unexpected system-level error has occurred during the lookup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must flag an error condition (Error Flag set to 'Y') to halt any further login processing and prevent unauthorized access

rules.rule_name: Set Error Message for Security System Verification Failure
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs during user verification, the system must communicate the failure to the user with a specific error message indicating that the system could not verify their identity.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Message: 'Unable to verify the User...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unexpected system error has been detected during the user security file lookup and the error condition flag has been set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the Sign-On screen response for the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the screen error message to 'Unable to verify the User ...' so the user is informed that the system encountered a problem verifying their credentials

rules.rule_name: Reposition Cursor to User ID Field on Verification Failure
rules.rule_description: When the system is unable to verify the user due to an unexpected security system error, the cursor must be repositioned to the User ID field to guide the user to re-enter their credentials from the beginning.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reposition Cursor to User ID Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unexpected system error has occurred during user verification and the error message 'Unable to verify the User ...' has been set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Sign-On screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must reposition the input cursor to the User ID field, prompting the user to re-enter their User ID first when retrying

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Sign-On Screen with Verification Error Message
rules.rule_description: After an unexpected security system error, the system must redisplay the Sign-On screen with the error message visible so the user can retry their login attempt.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Signon Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unexpected system error has occurred during user verification, the error flag is set to 'Y', the error message is set to 'Unable to verify the User ...', and the cursor is positioned on the User ID field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the response back to the user's terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must redisplay the Sign-On screen populated with the current date, time, application title, transaction name, program name, application ID, system ID, and the error message 'Unable to verify the User ...' — with the cursor placed on the User ID field — so the user is prompted to try again

rules.rule_name: Record Originating Transaction ID into User Session on Successful Login
rules.rule_description: Upon successful authentication, the system captures and stores the current transaction identifier into the user session context so that downstream programs know which transaction initiated the session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Transaction ID into User Session

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated with a valid User ID and matching Password found in the user security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the user session context after successful credential verification
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) must be recorded into the user session field CDEMO-FROM-TRANID to identify the originating transaction for the session

rules.rule_name: Record Originating Program Name into User Session on Successful Login
rules.rule_description: Upon successful authentication, the system captures and stores the current program name into the user session context so that downstream programs can identify which program initiated the session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Program Name into User Session

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated with a valid User ID and matching Password found in the user security file, and the Transaction ID has already been recorded into the session
acceptance_criteria.When: The system continues preparing the user session context after successful credential verification
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) must be recorded into the user session field CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM to identify the originating program for the session

rules.rule_name: Record Authenticated User ID into User Session on Successful Login
rules.rule_description: Upon successful authentication, the system stores the verified User ID into the shared user session context so that all downstream programs have access to the identity of the logged-in user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record User ID into User Session

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated with a valid User ID and matching Password found in the user security file, and the Transaction ID and Program Name have already been recorded into the session
acceptance_criteria.When: The system continues preparing the user session context after successful credential verification
acceptance_criteria.Then: The authenticated User ID (WS-USER-ID, already converted to uppercase) must be recorded into the user session field CDEMO-USER-ID to establish the identity of the active user across the session

rules.rule_name: Record User Type into User Session on Successful Login
rules.rule_description: Upon successful authentication, the system stores the user's type (e.g., Administrator or Regular User) from the security file into the shared user session context so that downstream programs can apply appropriate access controls and menu routing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record User Type into User Session

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated with a valid User ID and matching Password found in the user security file, and the Transaction ID, Program Name, and User ID have already been recorded into the session
acceptance_criteria.When: The system continues preparing the user session context after successful credential verification
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE) retrieved from the user security file must be recorded into the user session field CDEMO-USER-TYPE to establish the role of the active user for the session

rules.rule_name: Initialize Program Context to Zero on Successful Login
rules.rule_description: Upon successful authentication, the system resets the program context indicator to zero in the user session, ensuring that the user starts with a fresh navigation state with no prior program context carried over.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Initialize Program Context to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated and the Transaction ID, Program Name, User ID, and User Type have all been recorded into the user session context
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes the user session context preparation before routing the user to the appropriate menu
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program context field (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) in the user session must be set to zero (0), indicating a fresh start with no prior navigation context

rules.rule_name: Route Administrator User to CardDemo Administration Menu
rules.rule_description: After successful authentication and session context setup, the system evaluates the user's type. If the user is identified as an Administrator, control is transferred to the CardDemo Administration Menu program, passing the full user session information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is User an Administrator?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated, and the user session context has been fully populated with Transaction ID, Program Name, User ID, User Type, and Program Context reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Type stored in the session (CDEMO-USER-TYPE) and determines that the user is of Administrator type (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is true)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must transfer control to the CardDemo Administration Menu program (COADM01C), passing the complete user session data (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the Administration Menu is displayed to the Admin user

rules.rule_name: Route Regular User to CardDemo Regular User Menu
rules.rule_description: After successful authentication and session context setup, the system evaluates the user's type. If the user is NOT identified as an Administrator (i.e., a regular user), control is transferred to the CardDemo Regular User Menu program, passing the full user session information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Route to Regular User Menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated, and the user session context has been fully populated with Transaction ID, Program Name, User ID, User Type, and Program Context reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Type stored in the session (CDEMO-USER-TYPE) and determines that the user is NOT of Administrator type (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is false)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must transfer control to the CardDemo Regular User Menu program (COMEN01C), passing the complete user session data (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the Regular User Menu is displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Determine User Routing Based on User Type After Successful Login
rules.rule_description: After successful authentication and session context preparation, the system evaluates the authenticated user's type to determine which menu or program the user should be directed to — either the Admin Menu or the Regular User Main Menu.

acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Type stored in the session context
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the User Type indicates an Admin user, the system routes the user to the Admin Menu; if the User Type indicates a regular (non-admin) user, the system routes the user to the CardDemo Main Menu (COMEN01C)

rules.rule_name: Route Regular User to CardDemo Main Menu

Transfer Control to

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated with a valid User ID and matching password, the user session information has been populated (Transaction ID, Program Name, User ID, User Type, Program Context), and the User Type is identified as a regular (non-admin) user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the user is not an Admin and initiates the transfer to the main menu
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers full control to the CardDemo Main Menu program (COMEN01C), passing the complete user session communication area containing the authenticated User ID, User Type, originating Transaction ID, originating Program Name, and initialized Program Context — so that the main menu program receives all necessary user session details upon entry

acceptance_criteria.Given: The signon screen is displayed and the user has an active session (communication area exists)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key that is neither the ENTER key nor the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies the key press as unsupported and triggers the invalid key error handling process

rules.rule_name: Activate Error Flag on Invalid Key Press
rules.rule_description: When an unsupported key is pressed, the system marks the error state as active to signal that an error condition exists and must be communicated to the user.

acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects the unsupported key press

rules.rule_name: Load Invalid Key Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error flag has been set to active due to an unsupported key press
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the error response
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system loads the standard invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) from the application message definitions into the working message area

rules.rule_name: Populate Signon Screen Header with Current Date, Time and System Information
rules.rule_description: Before redisplaying the signon screen, the system populates the screen header with current date, current time, application titles, transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID to ensure the screen header reflects up-to-date contextual information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Screen Header Information

acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header population process is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the signon screen header with: (1) Application Title Line 1 from CCDA-TITLE01, (2) Application Title Line 2 from CCDA-TITLE02, (3) Current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, (4) Current time formatted as HH:MM:SS, (5) Current transaction name, (6) Current program name, (7) Application ID retrieved from the system, and (8) System ID retrieved from the system

rules.rule_name: Place Error Message on Signon Screen
rules.rule_description: The invalid key error message stored in the working message area is transferred to the error message display field on the signon screen so the user can see the reason for the error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Error Message on Signon Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The invalid key error message has been loaded into the working message area and the screen header has been populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the signon screen output
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system moves the error message from the working message area (WS-MESSAGE) into the error message output field (ERRMSGO) on the signon screen map

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Signon Screen with Invalid Key Error Message
rules.rule_description: After preparing the error message and header information, the system redisplays the signon screen to the user, clearing the previous screen content and showing the invalid key error message so the user can retry with a supported key.

rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 on the Sign-On screen, the system prepares a standard Thank You message to be displayed, signaling the intent to end the CardDemo session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Thank You Message for Display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the CardDemo Sign-On screen and has an active session (communication area exists)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the display message to the standard CardDemo Thank You message (CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU) in preparation for session termination

rules.rule_name: Display Thank You Message and End CardDemo Session
rules.rule_description: After the Thank You message is set, the system displays it as plain text on the screen and immediately terminates the CardDemo session without returning control back to the Sign-On transaction. No further interaction is possible after this point.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Thank You Message on Screen - CardDemo Session Ended

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Thank You message has been set and the user has pressed PF3 to exit the CardDemo application
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the session termination request
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the Thank You message as plain text on the screen, clears the screen (ERASE), releases the keyboard (FREEKB), and immediately ends the session without passing a transaction ID or communication area back — effectively terminating the CardDemo session permanently

key_functionalities.description: Exit Application with Thank You Message

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the CardDemo Sign-On application
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No prior session communication area exists (first-time launch)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system initializes the screen output area to low values, positions the cursor on the User ID field, and displays the Sign-On screen for the first time

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-001: Detect First-Time Application Launch
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the user is accessing the Sign-On screen for the first time (no active session exists) or returning after a prior interaction, and routes accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Sign-On screen is about to be displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for rendering
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), current Transaction Name (WS-TRANID), current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME), current date formatted as MM/DD/YY (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY), current time formatted as HH:MM:SS (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS), the Application ID (APPLID), and the System ID (SYSID)

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-002: Populate Sign-On Screen Header Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the Sign-On screen is rendered, the header section must be populated with current date, current time, application titles, transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header has been populated and any applicable error message has been set in WS-MESSAGE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Sign-On screen (COSGN0A / COSGN00) to the terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message field (ERRMSGO) on the screen is populated with WS-MESSAGE, the screen is sent with ERASE to clear prior content, the cursor is positioned as specified, and the system waits for the next user input

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-003: Display Sign-On Screen to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Sign-On screen is sent to the user's terminal with any error messages and cursor positioning applied, clearing the previous screen content before display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has an active session and is on the Sign-On screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses a key and the system receives the input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the key is ENTER, the system proceeds to validate the login credentials; if the key is PF3, the system displays a Thank You message and ends the session; if any other key is pressed, the system sets an error flag and displays the invalid key error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-004: Handle User Key Press Selection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a returning user interacts with the Sign-On screen, the system evaluates which key was pressed and routes to the appropriate processing path: ENTER for login, PF3 for exit, or any other key triggers an invalid key error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Sign-On screen with an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the standard Thank You message (CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU) as plain text on the screen, clears the screen (ERASE), releases the keyboard (FREEKB), and immediately ends the session with no further transaction return

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-005: Exit Application with Thank You Message on PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the Sign-On screen, the application displays a Thank You message and terminates the current session without returning to the Sign-On transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Sign-On screen with an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), populates WS-MESSAGE with the invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message shown in the ERRMSGO field

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-006: Handle Invalid Key Press on Sign-On Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3 on the Sign-On screen, the system rejects the action and informs the user that the key pressed is not valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user presses ENTER on the Sign-On screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID field (USERIDI of COSGN0AI) contains only spaces or low values (is blank or empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets WS-MESSAGE to 'Please enter User ID ...', positions the cursor on the User ID field (USERIDL = -1), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message; no further login processing occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-007: Validate User ID is Not Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: The User ID field is mandatory on the Sign-On screen. If the user submits the form without entering a User ID, the system must reject the submission and prompt the user to provide one.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user presses ENTER on the Sign-On screen and has entered a valid (non-blank) User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Password field (PASSWDI of COSGN0AI) contains only spaces or low values (is blank or empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets WS-MESSAGE to 'Please enter Password ...', positions the cursor on the Password field (PASSWDL = -1), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message; no further login processing occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-008: Validate Password is Not Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Password field is mandatory on the Sign-On screen. If the user submits the form with a valid User ID but without entering a Password, the system must reject the submission and prompt the user to provide one.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered both a non-blank User ID and a non-blank Password on the Sign-On screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the credentials for authentication
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID (USERIDI of COSGN0AI) is converted to uppercase and stored in both WS-USER-ID and CDEMO-USER-ID; the Password (PASSWDI of COSGN0AI) is converted to uppercase and stored in WS-USER-PWD; these uppercase values are used for all subsequent authentication processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-009: Normalize User Credentials to Uppercase
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before performing any authentication lookup, both the User ID and Password entered by the user are converted to uppercase to ensure case-insensitive credential matching.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has provided a non-blank User ID and Password, both have been normalized to uppercase, and no validation errors have been flagged (ERR-FLG-ON is false)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a lookup on the User Security File (WS-USRSEC-FILE) using WS-USER-ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the user's security record (SEC-USER-DATA) including the stored password (SEC-USR-PWD) and user type (SEC-USR-TYPE) for use in subsequent authentication steps

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-010: Look Up User in Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system retrieves the user's security record from the User Security File (USRSEC) using the normalized (uppercase) User ID as the lookup key, provided no prior validation errors have occurred.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup on the User Security File using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID is not found in the User Security File (response code = 13 / record not found)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets WS-MESSAGE to 'User not found. Try again ...', positions the cursor on the User ID field (USERIDL = -1), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-011: Handle User Not Found in Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the entered User ID does not exist in the User Security File, the system informs the user that the account was not found and prompts them to try again.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup on the User Security File using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The security file lookup returns an unexpected error (any response code other than success or record-not-found)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets WS-MESSAGE to 'Unable to verify the User ...', positions the cursor on the User ID field (USERIDL = -1), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-012: Handle Authentication System Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: If an unexpected condition occurs while attempting to retrieve the user's record from the security file, the system informs the user that verification could not be completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user's record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the entered password (WS-USER-PWD, already normalized to uppercase) against the stored password (SEC-USR-PWD) in the retrieved security record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the passwords match, the system proceeds to establish the user session and route the user; if the passwords do not match, the system displays a wrong password error

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-013: Verify User Password Against Stored Credentials
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user record is successfully found in the security file, the system compares the entered (uppercase) password against the stored password to authenticate the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user's record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered password (WS-USER-PWD) does not match the stored password (SEC-USR-PWD)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets WS-MESSAGE to 'Wrong Password. Try again ...', positions the cursor on the Password field (PASSWDL = -1), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message; no session is established

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-014: Handle Wrong Password Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user is found in the security file but the entered password does not match the stored password, the system rejects the login and prompts the user to try again.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user's record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File and the entered password matches the stored password
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Authentication is confirmed as successful
