Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the following in the shared session context (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA): the originating Transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID = WS-TRANID), the originating Program Name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM = WS-PGMNAME), the authenticated User ID (CDEMO-USER-ID = WS-USER-ID), the User Type (CDEMO-USER-TYPE = SEC-USR-TYPE), and the Program Context is reset to zero (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = 0)

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-015: Establish User Session Context on Successful Authentication
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful authentication (User ID found and password matches), the system records the session context information that will be passed to downstream application programs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated (User ID found and password matched) and the session context has been established
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user's type (CDEMO-USER-TYPE / SEC-USR-TYPE) is identified as ADMIN (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Administration Menu program (COADM01C), passing the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-016: Route Admin User to Administration Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successful authentication, if the user is identified as an Administrator, the system transfers control to the Administration Menu program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated (User ID found and password matched) and the session context has been established
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user's type (CDEMO-USER-TYPE / SEC-USR-TYPE) is NOT identified as ADMIN (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is false)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Regular User Main Menu program (COMEN01C), passing the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)

all_rules.Rule_Name: BR-017: Route Regular User to Main Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successful authentication, if the user is not an Administrator, the system transfers control to the Regular User Main Menu program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user initiates the CardDemo application transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No prior session communication area exists (the application has not been previously launched in this session)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies this as a first-time launch and proceeds to initialize and display the Signon screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect First-Time Application Launch
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the CardDemo signon screen is being accessed for the first time by checking if there is no existing session communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo application is being launched for the first time in a session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initializes the Signon screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All fields on the Signon screen output map (COSGN0AO) are set to blank/empty values, ensuring a clean login form is presented with no pre-filled data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Signon Screen with Blank Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: Clears all fields on the Signon screen output map to ensure no residual or stale data is displayed to the user on first launch.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo Signon screen is being displayed for the first time
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for user input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor is automatically positioned on the User ID input field so the user can immediately begin typing their User ID without manually clicking or tabbing to the field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Position Cursor on User ID Field at Initial Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures the cursor is automatically placed on the User ID input field when the Signon screen is first displayed, guiding the user to begin entry at the correct field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing the Signon screen header information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current date is retrieved from the system
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The date is formatted as MM/DD/YY where MM is the two-digit month, DD is the two-digit day, and YY is the two-digit year, and this formatted date is stored for display in the screen header field (CURDATEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve and Format Current Date for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Retrieves the current system date and formats it in MM/DD/YY format to be displayed in the Signon screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing the Signon screen header information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current time is retrieved from the system
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The time is formatted as HH:MM:SS where HH is hours, MM is minutes, and SS is seconds, and this formatted time is stored for display in the screen header field (CURTIMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve and Format Current Time for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Retrieves the current system time and formats it in HH:MM:SS format to be displayed in the Signon screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing the Signon screen header information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The application identifier is requested from the system environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Application ID is retrieved and stored in the screen header field (APPLIDO) for display on the Signon screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Application ID for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Retrieves the current application identifier from the system environment to be displayed in the Signon screen header, identifying which application instance the user is accessing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing the Signon screen header information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system identifier is requested from the system environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The System ID is retrieved and stored in the screen header field (SYSIDO) for display on the Signon screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve System ID for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Retrieves the current system identifier from the system environment to be displayed in the Signon screen header, identifying which system the user is connected to.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing the Signon screen header information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction name and program name are retrieved from the working session context
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Name is placed in the screen header field (TRNNAMEO) and the Program Name is placed in the screen header field (PGMNAMEO) for display on the Signon screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Transaction Name and Program Name in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Populates the Signon screen header with the current transaction name and program name to provide context about the active transaction and program being executed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing the Signon screen header information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header is being assembled with all required display elements
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed in the screen header field (TITLE01O) and Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed in the screen header field (TITLE02O) on the Signon screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Application Titles in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Populates the Signon screen header with the two application title lines defined in the CardDemo application constants, providing consistent branding across the application.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Signon screen has been fully initialized with blank input fields, cursor positioned on User ID, and the header populated with current date, time, Application ID, System ID, transaction name, program name, and application titles
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Signon screen to the user's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete Signon screen is displayed to the user with: (1) the User ID input field, (2) the Password input field, (3) the application header showing current date in MM/DD/YY format, current time in HH:MM:SS format, Application ID, System ID, Transaction Name, Program Name, and Application Titles; any previous screen content is cleared and the cursor is on the User ID field; the system then waits for user input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Signon Screen with Login Form and Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Sends the fully populated Signon screen to the user's terminal, displaying the login form with User ID and Password input fields along with the complete application header, clearing any previous screen content.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Sign-On screen header is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system retrieves the current system date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The date is formatted as MM/DD/YY (two-digit month, two-digit day, two-digit year) and placed in the Date field of the Sign-On screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Set Current Date on Sign-On Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the Sign-On screen, the system retrieves the current system date and formats it as MM/DD/YY to be displayed in the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Sign-On screen header is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system retrieves the current system time
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The time is formatted as HH:MM:SS (two-digit hours, two-digit minutes, two-digit seconds) and placed in the Time field of the Sign-On screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Set Current Time on Sign-On Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the Sign-On screen, the system retrieves the current system time and formats it as HH:MM:SS to be displayed in the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Sign-On screen header is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The header information is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction name is set in the Transaction Name field of the Sign-On screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Transaction Name on Sign-On Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the Sign-On screen, the current transaction name is placed in the Transaction Name field of the screen header to identify the active transaction to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Sign-On screen header is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The header information is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current program name is set in the Program Name field of the Sign-On screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Program Name on Sign-On Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the Sign-On screen, the current program name is placed in the Program Name field of the screen header to identify the active program to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Sign-On screen header is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system retrieves the Application ID from the runtime environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Application ID is set in the Application ID field of the Sign-On screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve and Set Application ID on Sign-On Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the Sign-On screen, the system retrieves the Application ID from the runtime environment and places it in the Application ID field of the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Sign-On screen header is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system retrieves the System ID from the runtime environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The System ID is set in the System ID field of the Sign-On screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve and Set System ID on Sign-On Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the Sign-On screen, the system retrieves the System ID from the runtime environment and places it in the System ID field of the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Sign-On screen header is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The header information is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Application Title Line 1 and Application Title Line 2 are set in the respective title fields of the Sign-On screen header using the standard application-defined title values

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Application Titles on Sign-On Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the Sign-On screen, the standard application titles (Title Line 1 and Title Line 2) defined in the application configuration are placed in the corresponding title fields of the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Sign-On screen is about to be displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population process completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Sign-On screen header contains all of the following populated fields: Application Title Line 1, Application Title Line 2, current date in MM/DD/YY format, current time in HH:MM:SS format, transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID — and the screen is ready to be sent to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Complete Screen Header Population Before Sign-On Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Sign-On screen must always be displayed with a fully populated header containing all required fields: application titles, current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID. All these fields must be populated before the screen is sent to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Sign-On screen and has pressed a key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed is the Enter key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to the login validation process to verify the user's entered credentials (User ID and Password)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route to Login Validation on Enter Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the Enter key on the Sign-On screen, the system initiates the login validation process to authenticate the user's credentials.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Sign-On screen and has pressed a key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed is PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the standard Thank You message (CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU) as plain text on the screen, the keyboard is unlocked for the user, and the application session is terminated — no further transaction processing occurs and the Sign-On screen is not redisplayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Thank You Message and End Session on PF3 Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the Sign-On screen, the system displays a Thank You message and terminates the current application session immediately without returning to the Sign-On screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Sign-On screen and has pressed a key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed is any key other than Enter or PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', populates the error message area on the Sign-On screen with the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message visible so the user can press a valid key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Invalid Key Error and Redisplay Sign-On Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses any key other than Enter or PF3 on the Sign-On screen, the system flags an error, displays an invalid key error message, and redisplays the Sign-On screen so the user can retry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An invalid key error has been flagged and the invalid key error message has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Sign-On screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with the current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID; the invalid key error message is placed in the error message field of the Sign-On screen; and the Sign-On screen is redisplayed with the error message visible, awaiting the next valid user input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Sign-On Screen with Invalid Key Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After an invalid key press is detected, the Sign-On screen is refreshed with updated header information (current date, time, application ID, system ID) and the invalid key error message displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has accessed the signon screen and presses the Enter key to submit their credentials
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID field submitted on the signon screen is empty or contains only blank spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system rejects the login attempt, sets an error indicator to active, displays the error message 'Please enter User ID ...', repositions the cursor to the User ID field, and redisplays the signon screen with the error message so the user can re-enter their credentials

all_rules.Rule_Name: User ID Presence Validation on Signon Screen Submission
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user submits the signon screen by pressing Enter, the system must verify that the User ID field has been filled in. If the User ID field is empty or contains only blank spaces, the submission is rejected and the user is prompted to provide a User ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the signon screen by pressing Enter
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID field is empty or blank
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error indicator flag to 'Y' (active/on), which prevents any downstream authentication or user lookup from being executed for this submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Activate Error Indicator on Missing User ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User ID field is found to be empty or blank upon signon screen submission, the system must activate an internal error indicator to signal that a validation failure has occurred, preventing any further authentication processing from taking place.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the signon screen by pressing Enter and the User ID field is empty or blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the missing User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system prepares the error message 'Please enter User ID ...' to be displayed on the signon screen so the user understands exactly what information is required

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User ID Missing Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User ID field is empty or blank on signon screen submission, the system must prepare and display a specific, user-friendly error message instructing the user to enter their User ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the signon screen by pressing Enter and the User ID field is empty or blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the signon screen with the error message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the cursor position to the User ID input field so that when the signon screen is redisplayed, the cursor is automatically placed in the User ID field, ready for the user to type their User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reposition Cursor to User ID Field on Validation Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User ID field is found to be empty or blank, the system must automatically reposition the screen cursor to the User ID input field to guide the user directly to the field that requires attention, improving the user experience.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has detected that the User ID field is empty or blank, set the error indicator, prepared the error message 'Please enter User ID ...', and positioned the cursor on the User ID field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the signon screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID, then displays the signon screen with the error message 'Please enter User ID ...' visible and the cursor positioned on the User ID field, awaiting the user's corrected input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Signon Screen with User ID Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After detecting a missing User ID and preparing the error message and cursor position, the system must redisplay the signon screen including the header information (current date, time, application details) along with the error message, so the user can correct their input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the signon screen by pressing Enter
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID field contains a non-blank, non-empty value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does not set an error for the User ID field and proceeds to validate whether the Password field has also been filled in

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Password Validation When User ID is Present
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User ID field contains a value (is not empty or blank), the signon screen submission passes the User ID validation check and the system proceeds to the next step of validating the Password field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has accessed the Sign-On screen and has pressed the ENTER key to submit the form, and the User ID field has already been validated as non-empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Password field submitted on the Sign-On screen contains only blank spaces or is empty (LOW-VALUES)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to indicate a validation failure, (2) display the error message 'Please enter Password...' on the Sign-On screen, (3) reposition the cursor to the Password field so the user can immediately enter their password, and (4) redisplay the Sign-On screen with the error message visible, awaiting re-entry from the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Password Field Mandatory Entry Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Password field is not left blank or empty when the user submits the Sign-On screen. This ensures the user provides a password before the system attempts to authenticate their credentials.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Sign-On screen by pressing ENTER, and the User ID field has passed its mandatory entry check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects that the Password field is blank or empty (contains only spaces or LOW-VALUES)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the internal error flag to 'Y' (error condition active), which will prevent any downstream credential lookup or authentication processing from being triggered for this submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Password Entry Error Flag Activation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Password field is found to be blank or empty upon form submission, the system activates an error flag to signal that a validation failure has occurred, preventing any further credential verification or authentication processing from taking place.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Sign-On screen by pressing ENTER with the Password field left blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system identifies the Password field as blank or empty and prepares to redisplay the Sign-On screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the error message to exactly 'Please enter Password...' and display this message in the error message area of the Sign-On screen so the user is clearly informed of what is required

all_rules.Rule_Name: Password Missing Error Message Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Password field is blank or empty, the system communicates a clear, user-friendly error message instructing the user to provide their password before resubmitting the Sign-On screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has detected that the Password field was blank or empty upon Sign-On screen submission
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Sign-On screen with the password validation error message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the cursor position indicator for the Password field to -1, which instructs the screen to place the cursor directly in the Password input field when the screen is redisplayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Repositioning to Password Field on Validation Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: To improve user experience and guide the user to correct the missing input, the system automatically repositions the cursor to the Password field when the password entry validation fails, allowing the user to immediately begin typing their password without manually clicking or tabbing to the field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has set the error flag, error message 'Please enter Password...', and cursor position to the Password field due to a blank password submission
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the screen redisplay process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) populate the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID; (2) place the error message 'Please enter Password...' in the error message display area of the Sign-On screen; (3) redisplay the full Sign-On screen with the cursor positioned on the Password field; and (4) return control to the Sign-On transaction, awaiting the user's next input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sign-On Screen Redisplay After Password Validation Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After detecting a missing password entry, the system redisplays the Sign-On screen with the error message and updated cursor position, allowing the user to correct their input and resubmit. The screen header is refreshed with current date, time, application, and system information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Sign-On screen by pressing ENTER, and both the User ID and Password fields contain non-blank, non-empty values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the Password field and determines it is not blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must allow processing to continue to the credential normalization step, where both the User ID and Password will be converted to uppercase in preparation for authentication against the user security records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Credential Normalization When Password is Present
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Password field contains a non-blank, non-empty value, the password validation check passes and the system proceeds to the next step of normalizing (converting to uppercase) both the User ID and Password before performing credential verification.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a User ID on the Signon Screen and pressed the ENTER key, and both the User ID and Password fields have been confirmed as non-blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the entered User ID prior to performing the security file lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system converts the entered User ID to uppercase and stores the normalized uppercase value as the active User ID to be used for all subsequent authentication processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert Entered User ID to Uppercase for Case-Insensitive Authentication
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must normalize the User ID entered on the signon screen by converting it to uppercase before any authentication or security lookup is performed, ensuring that login is case-insensitive regardless of how the user typed their credentials.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The entered User ID has been converted to uppercase
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the normalized User ID for use in authentication and session tracking
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The uppercase User ID is stored in both the local authentication working storage field and the shared session context User ID field, ensuring the same normalized value is used for the security file lookup and carried forward into the session upon successful login

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Uppercase User ID in Session Context for Downstream Use
all_rules.Rule_Description: After converting the User ID to uppercase, the system must store the normalized User ID in both the local authentication working area and the shared session context (communication area), so that the authenticated identity is consistently available to all downstream programs and menus after successful login.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a Password on the Signon Screen and pressed the ENTER key, and both the User ID and Password fields have been confirmed as non-blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the entered Password prior to performing the security file lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system converts the entered Password to uppercase and stores the normalized uppercase value as the active Password to be used for all subsequent authentication and password comparison processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert Entered Password to Uppercase for Case-Insensitive Authentication
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must normalize the Password entered on the signon screen by converting it to uppercase before comparing it against the stored password in the security file, ensuring that password validation is case-insensitive.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The entered Password has been converted to uppercase
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the normalized Password for use in authentication
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The uppercase Password is stored in the local authentication working storage field, and the system is ready to proceed to the security file lookup where this normalized password will be compared against the stored user password

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Uppercase Password for Authentication Comparison
all_rules.Rule_Description: After converting the Password to uppercase, the system must store the normalized Password in the local authentication working area so it is ready to be compared against the password stored in the user security file during the authentication lookup.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a valid non-blank User ID and Password on the Sign-On screen and pressed ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a lookup on the User Security File (USRSEC) using the uppercase-converted User ID as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the user record from the security file, which contains the stored password and user type, and proceeds to password verification

all_rules.Rule_Name: Search User Security File by User ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system uses the entered User ID as the lookup key to search the User Security File and retrieve the corresponding user record containing the stored password and user type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the User Security File using the entered User ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user record is found successfully in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the user record containing the stored password (SEC-USR-PWD) and the user type (SEC-USR-TYPE), and proceeds to password verification

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Record Successfully Retrieved from Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User Security File lookup is successful, the system retrieves the full user record including the stored password and user type classification, which are then used for authentication and role-based routing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the User Security File using the entered User ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No matching user record is found in the User Security File for the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'User not found. Try again...' on the Sign-On screen, repositions the cursor to the User ID field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen for re-entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: User ID Does Not Exist in Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered User ID cannot be found in the User Security File, the system rejects the login attempt, displays an appropriate error message, and prompts the user to re-enter their User ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to search the User Security File using the entered User ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security File returns an unexpected or unrecognized response (neither a successful retrieval nor a user-not-found result)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'Unable to verify the User...' on the Sign-On screen, repositions the cursor to the User ID field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen for re-entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Security File Cannot Be Accessed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User Security File is unavailable or returns an unexpected result during the user lookup, the system cannot verify the user's identity and displays an appropriate error message prompting the user to retry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the user security file using the entered User ID, and both the entered User ID and Password have been converted to uppercase prior to comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the uppercase-converted entered password (WS-USER-PWD) against the stored password (SEC-USR-PWD) retrieved from the user security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered password exactly matches the stored password, the system proceeds to prepare the user session information; if the passwords do not match, the system displays the error message 'Wrong Password. Try again...' and repositions the cursor to the Password field, then redisplays the Sign-On screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Password Verification Against Stored Credentials
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user record is successfully retrieved from the security file, the system compares the password entered by the user (converted to uppercase) against the stored password in the security file to determine whether authentication should proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The entered password has been verified and matches the stored password in the user security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the session context for the authenticated user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the following into the shared session communication area: the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is stored as the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), the current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) is stored as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), the authenticated User ID (WS-USER-ID) is confirmed and stored (CDEMO-USER-ID), the User Type from the security file (SEC-USR-TYPE) is stored (CDEMO-USER-TYPE), and the program context is reset to zero (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = 0)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare User Session Context Upon Successful Authentication
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful password verification, the system records all relevant session context information — including the originating transaction, program, authenticated user identity, and user type — into the shared communication area so that downstream programs can access this information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has been successfully authenticated and the session context has been fully populated with the user's transaction ID, program name, user ID, user type, and a reset program context
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the user type stored in the session context (CDEMO-USER-TYPE via CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the user type is identified as Administrator (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is true), the system routes the user to the Administration Menu; if the user type is not Administrator (regular user), the system routes the user to the Main Menu

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine User Role for Post-Login Routing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After session context is prepared, the system evaluates the authenticated user's type to determine whether the user holds an Administrator role, which governs which menu or application they are routed to after login.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has been successfully authenticated with a matching password, the session context has been populated, and the user type is identified as Administrator (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the user holds the Administrator role
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Administration Menu program (COADM01C), passing the current session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the current program terminates its execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Administrator User to Administration Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authenticated user is identified as an Administrator, the system transfers control to the Administration Menu program, passing the fully populated session communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has been successfully authenticated with a matching password, the session context has been populated, and the user type is NOT identified as Administrator (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is false)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the user is a regular (non-Administrator) user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Main Menu program (COMEN01C), passing the current session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the current program terminates its execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Regular User to Main Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authenticated user is identified as a regular (non-Administrator) user, the system transfers control to the Main Menu program, passing the fully populated session communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the user security file using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The uppercase-converted entered password (WS-USER-PWD) does NOT match the stored password (SEC-USR-PWD) in the security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the error message 'Wrong Password. Try again...' on the Sign-On screen, repositions the cursor to the Password input field (PASSWDL of COSGN0AI set to -1), and redisplays the Sign-On screen with the header information (current date, time, transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID) populated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Wrong Password Error Notification and Screen Re-prompt
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the password entered by the user does not match the stored password in the security file, the system notifies the user with a specific error message, repositions the cursor to the Password field to facilitate correction, and redisplays the Sign-On screen for another attempt.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a User ID and Password on the Sign-On screen and pressed ENTER, and both fields are non-blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a lookup of the entered User ID in the user security file and the User ID is NOT found (no matching record exists)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies that the User ID does not exist and initiates the 'User Not Found' error handling process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect User ID Not Found in Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user attempts to sign on, the system looks up the entered User ID in the security file. If the User ID does not exist, the system must detect this condition and trigger the appropriate error handling flow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the entered User ID in the user security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID is NOT found in the security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active ('Y'), marking the sign-on attempt as failed and blocking any further authentication processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Activate Error Flag on User Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User ID is not found in the security file, the system must activate the error flag to indicate that the current sign-on attempt has failed, preventing any further processing of the login.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that the entered User ID does not exist in the user security file and the error flag has been set to active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the error response for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error message to 'User not found. Try again ...' to be displayed on the Sign-On screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare User Not Found Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User ID entered by the user does not exist in the security file, the system must prepare a specific error message to inform the user that their User ID was not recognized and prompt them to try again.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that the entered User ID does not exist in the user security file and has prepared the error message 'User not found. Try again ...'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Sign-On screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system repositions the cursor to the User ID input field so the user can immediately re-enter a valid User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reposition Cursor to User ID Field on User Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User ID is not found in the security file, the system must reposition the screen cursor back to the User ID input field, guiding the user to correct their User ID entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has set the error flag to active, prepared the error message 'User not found. Try again ...', and repositioned the cursor to the User ID field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system redisplays the Sign-On screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system refreshes the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID; displays the error message 'User not found. Try again ...' in the error message area of the Sign-On screen; clears the screen and positions the cursor at the User ID field; and waits for the user to re-enter their credentials

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Sign-On Screen with User Not Found Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After detecting that the User ID does not exist, the system must redisplay the Sign-On screen with the error message visible, the screen header refreshed with current date and time, and the cursor positioned at the User ID field so the user can re-enter their credentials.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted their User ID and Password on the Sign-On screen and the system has attempted to look up the User ID in the user security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The security file returns a response that is neither a successful record found nor a record not found condition — indicating an unexpected system-level error has occurred during the lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must flag an error condition (Error Flag set to 'Y') to halt any further login processing and prevent unauthorized access

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Unexpected Security System Error During User Verification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user security file returns an unexpected or unrecognized response during a user lookup attempt, the system must flag an error condition to prevent further processing of the login request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unexpected system error has been detected during the user security file lookup and the error condition flag has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Sign-On screen response for the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the screen error message to 'Unable to verify the User ...' so the user is informed that the system encountered a problem verifying their credentials

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Error Message for Security System Verification Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs during user verification, the system must communicate the failure to the user with a specific error message indicating that the system could not verify their identity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unexpected system error has occurred during user verification and the error message 'Unable to verify the User ...' has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Sign-On screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must reposition the input cursor to the User ID field, prompting the user to re-enter their User ID first when retrying

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reposition Cursor to User ID Field on Verification Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system is unable to verify the user due to an unexpected security system error, the cursor must be repositioned to the User ID field to guide the user to re-enter their credentials from the beginning.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unexpected system error has occurred during user verification, the error flag is set to 'Y', the error message is set to 'Unable to verify the User ...', and the cursor is positioned on the User ID field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the response back to the user's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must redisplay the Sign-On screen populated with the current date, time, application title, transaction name, program name, application ID, system ID, and the error message 'Unable to verify the User ...' — with the cursor placed on the User ID field — so the user is prompted to try again

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Sign-On Screen with Verification Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After an unexpected security system error, the system must redisplay the Sign-On screen with the error message visible so the user can retry their login attempt.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated with a valid User ID and matching Password found in the user security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the user session context after successful credential verification
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) must be recorded into the user session field CDEMO-FROM-TRANID to identify the originating transaction for the session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Originating Transaction ID into User Session on Successful Login
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful authentication, the system captures and stores the current transaction identifier into the user session context so that downstream programs know which transaction initiated the session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated with a valid User ID and matching Password found in the user security file, and the Transaction ID has already been recorded into the session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues preparing the user session context after successful credential verification
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) must be recorded into the user session field CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM to identify the originating program for the session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Originating Program Name into User Session on Successful Login
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful authentication, the system captures and stores the current program name into the user session context so that downstream programs can identify which program initiated the session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated with a valid User ID and matching Password found in the user security file, and the Transaction ID and Program Name have already been recorded into the session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues preparing the user session context after successful credential verification
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authenticated User ID (WS-USER-ID, already converted to uppercase) must be recorded into the user session field CDEMO-USER-ID to establish the identity of the active user across the session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Authenticated User ID into User Session on Successful Login
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful authentication, the system stores the verified User ID into the shared user session context so that all downstream programs have access to the identity of the logged-in user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated with a valid User ID and matching Password found in the user security file, and the Transaction ID, Program Name, and User ID have already been recorded into the session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues preparing the user session context after successful credential verification
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE) retrieved from the user security file must be recorded into the user session field CDEMO-USER-TYPE to establish the role of the active user for the session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record User Type into User Session on Successful Login
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful authentication, the system stores the user's type (e.g., Administrator or Regular User) from the security file into the shared user session context so that downstream programs can apply appropriate access controls and menu routing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated and the Transaction ID, Program Name, User ID, and User Type have all been recorded into the user session context
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the user session context preparation before routing the user to the appropriate menu
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program context field (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) in the user session must be set to zero (0), indicating a fresh start with no prior navigation context

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Program Context to Zero on Successful Login
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful authentication, the system resets the program context indicator to zero in the user session, ensuring that the user starts with a fresh navigation state with no prior program context carried over.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated, and the user session context has been fully populated with Transaction ID, Program Name, User ID, User Type, and Program Context reset to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Type stored in the session (CDEMO-USER-TYPE) and determines that the user is of Administrator type (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must transfer control to the CardDemo Administration Menu program (COADM01C), passing the complete user session data (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the Administration Menu is displayed to the Admin user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Administrator User to CardDemo Administration Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successful authentication and session context setup, the system evaluates the user's type. If the user is identified as an Administrator, control is transferred to the CardDemo Administration Menu program, passing the full user session information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated, and the user session context has been fully populated with Transaction ID, Program Name, User ID, User Type, and Program Context reset to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Type stored in the session (CDEMO-USER-TYPE) and determines that the user is NOT of Administrator type (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is false)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must transfer control to the CardDemo Regular User Menu program (COMEN01C), passing the complete user session data (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the Regular User Menu is displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Regular User to CardDemo Regular User Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successful authentication and session context setup, the system evaluates the user's type. If the user is NOT identified as an Administrator (i.e., a regular user), control is transferred to the CardDemo Regular User Menu program, passing the full user session information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a valid User ID that exists in the security file and the entered password matches the stored password for that User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms successful credential verification and prepares the user session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must record the following session information: (1) Current Transaction ID is set to the Sign-On transaction identifier, (2) Current Program Name is set to the Sign-On program name, (3) Authenticated User ID is set to the verified user's ID (in uppercase), (4) User Type is set to the value retrieved from the security file record for that user, (5) Program Context is initialized to zero to indicate a fresh program start

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare User Session Information Upon Successful Authentication
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a user's credentials are successfully verified (User ID found and password matches), the system captures and stores the authenticated user's session information — including the originating transaction, program name, user identity, user type, and a freshly initialized program context — before routing the user to the appropriate menu.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated (User ID found and password verified) and the user session information has been prepared including the User Type retrieved from the security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Type stored in the session context
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the User Type indicates an Admin user, the system routes the user to the Admin Menu; if the User Type indicates a regular (non-admin) user, the system routes the user to the CardDemo Main Menu (COMEN01C)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine User Routing Based on User Type After Successful Login
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successful authentication and session context preparation, the system evaluates the authenticated user's type to determine which menu or program the user should be directed to — either the Admin Menu or the Regular User Main Menu.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has been successfully authenticated with a valid User ID and matching password, the user session information has been populated (Transaction ID, Program Name, User ID, User Type, Program Context), and the User Type is identified as a regular (non-admin) user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the user is not an Admin and initiates the transfer to the main menu
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers full control to the CardDemo Main Menu program (COMEN01C), passing the complete user session communication area containing the authenticated User ID, User Type, originating Transaction ID, originating Program Name, and initialized Program Context — so that the main menu program receives all necessary user session details upon entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Regular User to CardDemo Main Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a successfully authenticated user is identified as a regular (non-admin) user, the system transfers full control to the CardDemo Main Menu program, passing along the complete user session information so that downstream programs can identify the user, their type, and the originating transaction context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The signon screen is displayed and the user has an active session (communication area exists)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key that is neither the ENTER key nor the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies the key press as unsupported and triggers the invalid key error handling process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Unsupported Key Press on Signon Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3 on the signon screen, the system identifies it as an unsupported action and initiates error handling.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed an unsupported key on the signon screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the unsupported key press
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active ('Y') to indicate an error condition is present

all_rules.Rule_Name: Activate Error Flag on Invalid Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unsupported key is pressed, the system marks the error state as active to signal that an error condition exists and must be communicated to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error flag has been set to active due to an unsupported key press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the error response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system loads the standard invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) from the application message definitions into the working message area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load Invalid Key Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unsupported key is pressed, the system loads the standard invalid key error message from the application message repository to inform the user that the key they pressed is not supported.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to redisplay the signon screen after an invalid key press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population process is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the signon screen header with: (1) Application Title Line 1 from CCDA-TITLE01, (2) Application Title Line 2 from CCDA-TITLE02, (3) Current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, (4) Current time formatted as HH:MM:SS, (5) Current transaction name, (6) Current program name, (7) Application ID retrieved from the system, and (8) System ID retrieved from the system

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Signon Screen Header with Current Date, Time and System Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before redisplaying the signon screen, the system populates the screen header with current date, current time, application titles, transaction name, program name, application ID, and system ID to ensure the screen header reflects up-to-date contextual information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The invalid key error message has been loaded into the working message area and the screen header has been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the signon screen output
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves the error message from the working message area (WS-MESSAGE) into the error message output field (ERRMSGO) on the signon screen map

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Error Message on Signon Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The invalid key error message stored in the working message area is transferred to the error message display field on the signon screen so the user can see the reason for the error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The signon screen map has been populated with the invalid key error message in the error message field and the header has been populated with current date, time, and system information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the signon screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears the current screen (ERASE) and redisplays the full signon screen (map COSGN0A from mapset COSGN00) including the invalid key error message, with the cursor positioned as last set, allowing the user to retry their action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Signon Screen with Invalid Key Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After preparing the error message and header information, the system redisplays the signon screen to the user, clearing the previous screen content and showing the invalid key error message so the user can retry with a supported key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the CardDemo Sign-On screen and has an active session (communication area exists)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the display message to the standard CardDemo Thank You message (CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU) in preparation for session termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Thank You Message on PF3 Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the Sign-On screen, the system prepares a standard Thank You message to be displayed, signaling the intent to end the CardDemo session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Thank You message has been set and the user has pressed PF3 to exit the CardDemo application
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the session termination request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the Thank You message as plain text on the screen, clears the screen (ERASE), releases the keyboard (FREEKB), and immediately ends the session without passing a transaction ID or communication area back — effectively terminating the CardDemo session permanently

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Thank You Message and End CardDemo Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Thank You message is set, the system displays it as plain text on the screen and immediately terminates the CardDemo session without returning control back to the Sign-On transaction. No further interaction is possible after this point.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Sign-On screen is displayed and the user has pressed the Enter key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Sign-On screen input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures the values entered in the User ID field and the Password field from the screen for further validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive User Credentials from Sign-On Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses the Enter key on the Sign-On screen, the system captures the User ID and Password entered by the user from the screen input fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key on the Sign-On screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID field is blank or empty (contains spaces or low values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'Please enter User ID ...', repositions the cursor to the User ID field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen. The login attempt does not proceed further.

all_rules.Rule_Name: User ID Mandatory Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system enforces that the User ID field must be populated before a login attempt can proceed. If the User ID is blank or empty, the login attempt is rejected with an appropriate error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key on the Sign-On screen and the User ID field has been successfully validated as non-blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Password field is blank or empty (contains spaces or low values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'Please enter Password ...', repositions the cursor to the Password field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen. The login attempt does not proceed further.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Password Mandatory Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system enforces that the Password field must be populated before a login attempt can proceed. If the Password is blank or empty, the login attempt is rejected with an appropriate error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a non-blank User ID and a non-blank Password on the Sign-On screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Both the User ID and Password fields pass the mandatory field validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system converts the entered User ID to uppercase and stores it as the active User ID for the session lookup. The system also converts the entered Password to uppercase for subsequent password matching. The uppercase User ID is also stored in the shared session communication area.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Uppercase Conversion of User Credentials
all_rules.Rule_Description: To ensure case-insensitive authentication, the system converts both the User ID and Password to uppercase before performing any lookup or comparison against stored credentials.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User ID and Password have been validated as non-blank and converted to uppercase
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a lookup of the User Security File using the uppercase User ID as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the user's security record from the User Security File if the User ID exists, or returns an appropriate status indicating the user was not found or a system error occurred

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Identity Lookup in Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system searches the User Security File using the uppercase User ID to retrieve the user's stored security record, including stored password and user type, for authentication purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the User Security File using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID is not found in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'User not found. Try again ...', repositions the cursor to the User ID field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen. The login attempt is rejected.

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Not Found in Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the entered User ID does not exist in the User Security File, the system rejects the login attempt and prompts the user to try again.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to search the User Security File using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: An unexpected system condition occurs during the user lookup that is neither a successful retrieval nor a 'user not found' condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'Unable to verify the User ...', repositions the cursor to the User ID field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen. The login attempt is rejected.

all_rules.Rule_Name: System Unable to Verify User Identity
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the system encounters an unexpected condition while attempting to verify the user's identity in the Security File, the login attempt is rejected and the user is informed that verification could not be completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User ID has been found in the User Security File and the user's security record has been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the uppercase-converted entered password against the stored password in the user's security record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the passwords do not match, the system displays the message 'Wrong Password. Try again ...', repositions the cursor to the Password field, and redisplays the Sign-On screen. The login attempt is rejected. If the passwords match, the system proceeds to establish the user session.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Password Match Validation Against Stored Credentials
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the user record is successfully retrieved from the Security File, the system validates that the password entered by the user matches the password stored in the user's security record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has been successfully authenticated with a matching User ID and Password
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Authentication is confirmed as successful
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the following session information in the shared communication area: the originating Transaction ID, the originating Program Name, the authenticated User ID, the User Type (Admin or Regular), and resets the Program Context to zero to indicate a fresh program start

all_rules.Rule_Name: Establish User Session Information on Successful Authentication
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful authentication, the system records the user's session context information in the shared communication area so that downstream programs can identify the authenticated user and their role throughout the session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has been successfully authenticated and the session context has been established
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user's type stored in the Security File is identified as Administrator (Admin)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Administration Menu program (COADM01C), passing the full session communication area, so the Admin user can access administrative functions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Authenticated Admin User to Administration Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successful authentication, if the user is identified as an Administrator, the system routes them to the Administration Menu program, passing the established session context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has been successfully authenticated and the session context has been established
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user's type stored in the Security File is identified as a Regular user (non-Admin)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Main Menu program (COMEN01C), passing the full session communication area, so the Regular user can access standard application functions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Authenticated Regular User to Main Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successful authentication, if the user is identified as a Regular (non-Admin) user, the system routes them to the Main Menu program, passing the established session context.

description:
COSGN00C is the Signon Screen program for the CardDemo application that handles user authentication by accepting a User ID and Password, validating them against a security file, and routing authenticated users to the appropriate menu based on their user type (Admin or Regular user). The program displays the signon screen, processes user credentials, and upon successful authentication transfers control to either the Admin menu (COADM01C) or the regular user menu (COMEN01C). It is a Main/Driver program that initiates the CardDemo application session.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM/CICS File - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Display Signon Screen - Display the initial CardDemo application signon screen to the user when the application is first launched, showing the login form with User ID and Password fields along with application header information including current date, time, application ID, system ID, transaction name, and program name 2: Populate Screen Header Information - Retrieve and populate the screen header with current date (MM/DD/YY format), current time (HH:MM:SS format), application ID, system ID, transaction name, and program name before displaying the signon screen 3: Handle User Keypress - Evaluate the key pressed by the user on the signon screen: process Enter key for login attempt, process PF3 key for application exit, or display an invalid key error message for any other key pressed 4: Validate User ID Entry - Check if the User ID field is blank or empty when the user submits the signon screen; if empty, display an error message prompting the user to enter a User ID and reposition the cursor to the User ID field 5: Validate Password Entry - Check if the Password field is blank or empty when the user submits the signon screen; if empty, display an error message prompting the user to enter a Password and reposition the cursor to the Password field 6: Normalize User Credentials to Uppercase - Convert the entered User ID and Password to uppercase to ensure case-insensitive authentication before performing the security lookup 7: Look Up User in Security File - Search the user security file using the entered User ID as the key to retrieve the stored user record containing the user's password and user type 8: Verify User Password - Compare the password entered by the user against the stored password in the user security file; if they match, proceed with login; if they do not match, display a 'Wrong Password' error message and prompt the user to try again 9: Handle User Not Found - If the User ID does not exist in the security file, display a 'User not found' error message and reposition the cursor to the User ID field for the user to re-enter credentials 10: Handle Authentication System Error - If the security file cannot be accessed or an unexpected error occurs during user lookup, display an 'Unable to verify the User' error message and prompt the user to try again 11: Route Admin User to Administration Menu - After successful authentication, if the user is identified as an administrator type, transfer control to the CardDemo Administration menu program (COADM01C) passing the user session information 12: Route Regular User to Main Menu - After successful authentication, if the user is identified as a regular (non-admin) user, transfer control to the CardDemo main menu program (COMEN01C) passing the user session information 13: Handle Invalid Key Press - When the user presses an unsupported key on the signon screen, display an invalid key error message and redisplay the signon screen 14: Exit Application with Thank You Message - When the user presses PF3 to exit, display a thank-you message and return control, effectively ending the CardDemo session
